title: Majority Element
description:
One value in nums occupies more than half of its positions. Return that value. Such a majority is guaranteed to exist.

Think of unlike values canceling in pairs. Because the majority outnumbers all other values combined, it cannot be completely canceled; this observation leads to a constant-space solution rather than a frequency table.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [3,2,3]
Output: 3

Example 2:

Input: nums = [2,2,1,1,1,2,2]
Output: 2

Example 3:

Input: nums = [-4]
Output: -4

Constraints:

  • 1 <= nums.length <= 50,000
  • -1,000,000,000 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000
  • Some value occurs strictly more than nums.length / 2 times.

exampleTestCases.explanation: Four of the seven values are 2.
The sole value is automatically a majority.
